title: Intraoperative VIM thalamus microelectrode recordings during transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS) for essential tremor (Luu et al.; derivative: authors' processed 48 kHz signals)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the ventral intermediate (VIM) thalamus of nine adults with medication-refractory essential tremor undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. At each recording depth, 60 s were recorded with and without transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS), a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation therapy applied to the treated hand. This derivative repackages the authors' processed 48 kHz signals into BIDS (BrainVision format), with depth, stimulation settings and motion-artifact masks provided as metadata and events.
methods_description: Recordings were made with FHC Guideline 4000 LP+ at 48 kHz from anterior, center and posterior Ben-gun microelectrodes, each referenced bipolar to a macro contact. For each trial, 60 s were recorded with TAPS off and with TAPS on. The authors' processing applied software low-pass filtering, offset removal, trimming to 60 s and motion-artifact mask computation. The processed signals were then converted to BrainVision float32.
